UX Case Study · 2021

Kinetic

One member app, many gym brands: from booking a class to unlocking the door.

RoleProduct Designer (UX + UI + design system)
ClientNordic gym-management software provider
ScopeRelease 1.0 → Release 2.0
Built bySoftware studio (my employer)
Mohamed Nishaz · Product Design01
At a glance

A white-label app that lets gym members book, buy and get in, for every gym brand on one platform.

The problem

The client’s software runs hundreds of gyms, but members could only book through the web or at reception. Each gym chain wanted its own app, and the client couldn’t afford to build one per brand.

My role

I owned UX and UI across two releases: flows, high-fidelity screens, edge states, the themeable design system, and annotated dev files. I worked with the client’s product owner through weekly approval rounds.

What changed

Release 1.0 brought class booking to mobile. Release 2.0 made the app a full sales channel: memberships, services, value cards and products, plus keyless Bluetooth door entry.

Kinetic02
01 · Why this was worth solving

Members lived on their phones. Their gym didn’t.

For the client, every booking made by phone call or at the front desk cost staff time. Every membership not sold online was revenue left with competitors who already had slick apps.

But the client sells software, not a gym brand. Whatever we built had to look like it belonged to each gym that used it.

For members

Find a class, grab a spot and get in the door, in seconds, without queueing at reception.

For gym chains

An app with their name, colours and imagery that also sells memberships and products.

For the client

One codebase and one design system, configured per customer instead of rebuilt.

For front-desk staff

Fewer booking calls, fewer no-shows and an automatic waiting list.

The design challenge: one product that feels personal to every brand and stays simple for every member.

Kinetic03
02 · How I decided what to focus on

Three principles that guided every trade-off.

01

Brand lives in slots, not layouts

Logo, header image, header text and one accent colour are configurable. Everything else is fixed. When the client hit technical limits on per-brand theming, we let each customer pick from a vetted palette rather than any colour.

02

Status before details

Members open the app to answer one question: am I in? Booked, In queue and Fully booked are colour-coded tiles you can read at a glance. If a class starts within 3 hours, the app opens straight on My Bookings (a client requirement).

03

Rules visible, not buried

Booking windows, late-cancel penalties and waiting-list cut-offs caused most front-desk disputes. I surfaced them in the flow where they apply, with the full policy one tap away.

03 · White-label system

Same app, different gym. Proved with 14 brands.

Before building screens, I stress-tested the header against 14 real-world logo shapes: wordmarks, round badges, stacked marks, light on dark and dark on light.

  • Logo safe zone sized for wide and tall marks
  • Gradient overlay keeps text readable on any header photo
  • Header text capped at 50 characters, with categories sorted by the gym

Logos are blurred for NDA.

04 · Getting in

A fast way in, plus a guest mode for people who aren’t members yet.

Branded splash
Login
Explore (Release 2.0)
  • Email + password login, with a provider code or deep link for members whose gym isn’t pre-selected
  • SMS code autofill: the 6-digit code appears above the keyboard as soon as the field is focused
  • Guest mode (Release 2.0) lets people browse classes and the info tab, and be invited to join only when they try to book
  • Explore shows the brand header and featured categories. The “Unlock door” banner appears when the phone is near an entrance

05 · Core flow · Release 1.0

Book a class in three taps.

1 · Pick a day
2 · Check the details
3 · Booked
  • Week strip: the date in focus follows the card in the middle of the screen as you scroll
  • Status tiles on the right edge of each card: teal for Booked, pink for In queue
  • Spots-left pill (“05 spots left”) creates gentle urgency without a countdown
  • Sticky CTA keeps Join class in reach on long detail pages
  • Confirmation repeats only what matters: class, date, time and instructor
Kinetic07
06 · Edge cases

When the class is full.

The waiting list was the most rule-heavy part of the product. I mapped every state before designing a single tile:

  • Fully booked: the CTA becomes “Join waiting list” and the reason is shown above it
  • In queue: the status tile turns pink in My Bookings and Classes
  • Spot opens: the tile flips from In queue to Booked automatically
  • List closes before class starts. If no spot opened, the booking quietly drops
  • Subscription limit passed and cancelled class states, each with their own message
Fully booked

07 · Craft in the details

Rules in plain words. Empty screens that point somewhere.

Booking rules
No bookings yet
Offline

The three biggest sources of front-desk arguments (when booking opens, late cancels and waiting-list timing) were rewritten as three short, scannable blocks with an icon each.

  • Empty states always offer one next action (Explore, Try again), never a dead end
  • Error tone: the network error uses the accent red for the button, not for the whole screen
  • Chart empty states depend on tenure: a 1-week member sees weeks, not empty months and years
Kinetic09
08 · Iteration

Profile: from a stats page to a member’s wallet.

Release 1.0
Release 2.0

In 1.0, Profile was mostly visit statistics. Once Release 2.0 added purchases, members needed one place to see what they own.

  • Profile-completion ring and banner (“2 more steps…”) nudge new sign-ups to finish their profile without blocking them
  • Initials avatar when no photo exists, instead of an empty grey circle
  • Value cards show balance and expiry, and subscriptions show the next payment, so members stop asking reception
  • Logout moved from the header into Settings, a safer place for a destructive action
Kinetic10
09 · Release 2.0 · Sign up and subscribe

Joining a gym, fully on the phone.

1 · Home facility
2 · Identity
3 · Direct debit
  • Progress bar at the top of every step, so a long legal flow feels finite
  • Facility first: it decides which memberships and prices appear. If a gym has only one facility, the step is skipped
  • National ID with an escape hatch: a checkbox for people without one opens a manual-details path
  • Direct-debit consent says why bank details are needed before asking for them
  • Existing email is caught early (“An account already exists. Login?”), not at payment
Kinetic11
10 · One checkout for everything

Memberships, add-ons and protein bars in one cart.

Release 2.0 added four ways to buy. Instead of four checkouts, I designed one confirm screen that every purchase flow ends in.

  • “Pay today” vs bound period are separated, so recurring costs aren’t mistaken for today’s charge
  • Value cards and coupons apply inline as discount rows, and a personal value card is offered proactively
  • Itemised receipt with seller, VAT and payment method, ready for expense claims

11 · Release 2.0 · Services & value cards

Book a court, buy a 10-pack, gift a card.

Filter services
Service detail
Value cards
  • Services (courts, PT, massage) reuse the class-detail layout, with a quantity picker and a fixed price row added
  • Filter-first: service type → facility → time, each a single-select list with Reset
  • Value cards share one card component: preset bundles plus a custom-amount card
  • Gifting: a “someone else” recipient branch added receiver details without a separate flow

12 · Release 2.0 · Keyless entry

The phone is the key card.

The most hardware-dependent flow in the app. It had to work at the door, in a hurry, sometimes with a gym bag in one hand.

1

Proximity banner on Explore: “Unlock door. Please stand close to a door”

2

Nearest doors listed by name (entrance or exit). The closest one is pre-selected

3

Slide to unlock instead of a button, so a pocket tap can’t open a door by accident

Connecting
Choose door · slide
Kinetic14
13 · Design system

Built to be re-skinned. Documented so it stays that way.

Atomic naming (atom / mol / org) matched the dev component tree. Semantic colours (Booked, In queue, Error) never change per brand, so only the primary slot does. Buttons cover enabled, disabled and error states, plus the slide-to-unlock control and stepper.

Kinetic15
14 · Outcome & reflection

What changed because I was there.

Outcome

  • Release 1.0 (class booking, waiting list, profile) and Release 2.0 (8 commerce and access flows) delivered as dev-ready, annotated files
  • Every screen approved in weekly sign-off rounds with the client’s product owner
  • One themeable system replaced the idea of one app per gym brand
  • Booking and waiting-list rules moved from the front desk into the product

What I learned

Map the rules before the screens. The waiting list had more states than any visual design problem, and drawing them first stopped late surprises in development.

Constraints can be a feature. A curated palette protected contrast and accessibility across brands better than a free colour picker would have.

Next time

I’d set success metrics with the client up front, such as share of bookings made in the app, no-show rate and online membership sales, and run a short usability test on the checkout before handoff.

Thank you.
